solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Softie travelling about freezing point on new snow

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
something travelling moves about, so the letters of softie are shifted into a new order

parts.note: FP is the standard abbreviation for freezing point

explanation.surface: A soft skier heading off around the frost line onto fresh powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Softie' looks like a timid skier but is just letters: 'travelling' makes OFISTE, and 'about' sets it round the scientific shorthand FP.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing away from groomed runs means skiing through fresh, ungroomed powder, so an adjective for that terrain fits.

clue.text: Through which one can leave in a hurry to cool off

definitions.text: Through which one can leave in a hurry
definitions.meaning: an emergency door used to escape a building quickly
read whimsically as a blaze departing, which would make things cooler

explanation.surface: A way to slip out fast when things get heated.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a pun: when a fire exits, the room cools off.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency door is the route people take when they must escape a building quickly.

clue.text: Steps into the money during plague

indicators.note: into means the steps are placed inside the money

parts.note: pence is British money, the small coins
a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Someone climbing into wealth while an epidemic rages.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is a set of steps over a field wall, common in the British countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence is an old word for a deadly epidemic disease, a synonym of plague.

clue.text: Design gun by one in Sri Lanka

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the country code

parts.note: CL is the international vehicle registration code for Sri Lanka (from Ceylon)
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A weapon design being drawn up beside one in Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: CL survives from Sri Lanka's former name, Ceylon.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out pattern or the decorative pattern produced by it, so it is a design.

clue.text: Place in Greater London, not a place in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: not means the letter named after it is left out

parts.note: Earith is a village in Cambridgeshire
a gives the letter to be dropped

explanation.surface: A geography quiz contrasting a London suburb with a Cambridgeshire village.
explanation.walkthrough: Erith is a town in the London Borough of Bexley; Earith is a village near Huntingdon. 'not a' drops the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Erith is a town in south-east London, part of the Bexley borough of the metropolis.

clue.text: Clearly evident forgetting Long Island was omitted

indicators.note: was omitted tells us the named letters are dropped

parts.note: oblivious means unaware or forgetful

explanation.surface: Something plain to see, despite Long Island being left off the list.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious means plain to see or apparent, a direct synonym of clearly evident.

clue.text: Strive for high things, a High Church feature

parts.note: a spire is a tall pointed tower on a church, hence high

explanation.surface: Ambition likened to the lofty spire of a High Church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Church' looks like the Anglican tradition, but here the church feature is simply tall.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's ambitions on lofty goals, to strive for something great.

clue.text: Gallant seven times a week on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, so the word for seven times a week is given by its sound

parts.note: every night of the week, so nightly

explanation.surface: A chivalrous presenter who broadcasts every day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights were bound by chivalry, so behaving like one means being chivalrous and courteous.

clue.text: Book of Daniel

parts.note: not the Old Testament book but a novel by Daniel Defoe

explanation.surface: A reference to the Old Testament book of the prophet Daniel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible book is the false trail; the Daniel meant is Daniel Defoe, author of the 1719 castaway novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's most famous novel, about a shipwrecked sailor, is named after its hero.

clue.text: See 9
Fault-finding fool making a selection

parts.note: nit is British slang for a fool, short for nitwit
picking means choosing or selecting

explanation.surface: A critic dismissed as a fool for being so choosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty criticism of minor details is a fussy, carping sort of fault-finding.

clue.text: Cry out when I penetrate old shellfish

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: penetrate means the letter goes inside the shellfish

parts.note: a clam is a bivalve shellfish

explanation.surface: Shouting as one prises open an ancient clam.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to shout or utter something suddenly, as in surprise.

clue.text: Question in Hawaiian Island about Chilean shrub

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation is placed inside the island's name

parts.note: Maui is one of the Hawaiian islands

explanation.surface: A query raised in Hawaii concerning a South American plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The maqui is an evergreen bush native to Chile, known for its dark edible berries.

clue.text: Patient under obligation

definitions.meaning: a person undergoing treatment or experiment, such as a test case
bound by or liable to something, as one owing allegiance

explanation.surface: A sick person who still owes a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case in medicine is a patient; a person liable to a ruler or rule is bound to it.

clue.text: Ugly view?

definitions.meaning: a fright, as in 'you look a fright'
a scene that is seen, such as the local attractions

explanation.surface: An unattractive vista.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone looks a fright means they look terrible; a vista is something seen.

clue.text: Minister's game

definitions.meaning: belonging to Jack Straw, a Labour cabinet minister
a children's pastime of lifting thin sticks one by one from a pile

explanation.surface: A government minister's tactics or pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was British Home Secretary and Foreign Secretary; the possessive splits off his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Also called spillikins, it is a pastime of removing sticks from a heap without disturbing the rest.

clue.text: Individual entering Asian country or Irish county

indicators.note: entering means the single letter goes inside the country's name

parts.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia
I, the Roman one, is a single individual

explanation.surface: A single traveller entering a land, either Asian or Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: Laois is a county in the Irish midlands, in the province of Leinster.

clue.text: Amend? An hour later

definitions.meaning: one o'clock, an hour after noon

explanation.surface: A question about correcting something, put off for an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to atone; one o'clock is an hour later than twelve.

clue.text: Everybody seasoning berries

parts.note: all means every person
a spice is a flavouring used in cooking

explanation.surface: Everyone uses berries to season their food.
explanation.definitionFit: The pimento tree's dried fruit is the aromatic product; the spice is the ground berries.

clue.text: Shabby state in Seychelles

indicators.note: in means the state goes inside the country code

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A run-down condition found in the Seychelles islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a condition paired with 'Shabby', but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaly is informal slang for mean, scruffy or contemptible, close to shabby.

clue.text: Unknown boy first had nothing steady

indicators.note: first means the boy comes ahead of the unknown

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Y is an algebraic unknown
love means nil, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: An unknown lad started out with nothing stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steady' is a noun here, as in 'going steady'.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular sweetheart, a long-standing girlfriend.

clue.text: Second under-secretary has welcome dish

parts.note: US is an abbreviation for under-secretary
hi is a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A junior civil servant greets someone with a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese meal of vinegared rice with raw fish is a dish.

clue.text: Shut off Henry not appearing in revised schedule

indicators.note: not appearing means the named letter is missing from the fodder
revised means the timetable's letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An item cut from a rewritten timetable after someone dropped out.
explanation.definitionFit: To seclude is to isolate or keep apart from others, to shut off.

clue.text: During the commotion I zeroed in on electrical apparatus

indicators.note: during means the letters run within the following words

explanation.surface: Amid the chaos, someone homed in on a piece of electrical kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that charges air particles electrically is a piece of electrical equipment.

clue.text: The Spanish oiler went round this on the Rhine

indicators.note: went round suggests turning about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish tanker steaming round a famous Rhine landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went round' turns ELOILER into the answer; 'this' points to the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock on the Rhine is famed in legend as the haunt of a siren luring boatmen.

clue.text: On which it is publicly known as the best yet

definitions.text: On which it is publicly known
definitions.meaning: if it is on this, it is officially stated and known
an unbeaten best performance, such as a world best

explanation.surface: Something officially public, and also the finest so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'on record' means publicly stated; a world best is the top achievement so far.

clue.text: Cut deposit out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to remove a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb but is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This lean joint of beef from the upper hind leg is a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Fruit's soft and round

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit; the 's is not a letter
p is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A description of a ripe fruit, soft and rounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump means chubby or full in shape, so rounded.

clue.text: Select a flower aloud with relish

indicators.note: aloud means the phrase is to be heard, giving the answer by sound

parts.note: pick means select and a lily is a flower

explanation.surface: Choosing a bloom with great enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like enjoyment but is the condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: This mustard-flavoured pickle of chopped vegetables is a condiment, a relish.

clue.text: Simon to laze all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Simon likes to idle about everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon is one of the twelve apostles, called Simon the Zealot to distinguish him from Simon Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle was known by this epithet, naming him after a fanatical Jewish faction.

clue.text: Abrasive mound cur removed

indicators.note: removed means shifted from place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rough dog taken off a heap of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrasive' suggests a rude manner, but it means a grinding material.
explanation.definitionFit: This very hard mineral, aluminium oxide, is used for grinding and polishing.

clue.text: One dying to be a naughty child

definitions.meaning: British slang for a mischievous little rascal

explanation.surface: A dying person who is also a little terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who perishes is literally one dying; in British slang it is also an affectionate term for a brat.
